verdict_reason: The fixes resolve all thirteen findings, including the three majors (F1, F2, F3), and I re-checked each one in the main checkout. The new edits add no contradiction to the maxim. Three minor points and two nits remain (R1 to R5), mostly plan allowed_paths gaps the fixes exposed. None of them weakens the founding commitment or the plan graph, so none blocks acceptance.
method_and_limits: Read-only review. I ran no commands.

Files re-read: docs/ADOPTION_AND_GOVERNANCE.md, docs/ABI_AND_WRAPPERS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/QUALIFICATION.md, docs/TOOLCHAIN.md, engineering/plan.json (FP-0017 to FP-0023 and FP-0029), engineering/state.json, engineering/HANDOFF.md, engineering/workstreams.json, README.md, AGENT_LAUNCH.md, book/src/index.md, .omp/agents/fairpane-review.md, .omp/agents/fairpane-platform.md, and ADR 0001 and ADR 0004.
I also re-grepped every document for 'public C ABI', 'Zig API', and 'direct Zig' to catch new contradictions.

finding_status.evidence: docs/ADOPTION_AND_GOVERNANCE.md:44-45 now separates release-blocking decisions from the wrapper-language selection. That selection now 'blocks task `FP-0029` and every task that depends on it, starting with the browser shell in `FP-0017`.'

The FP-0021 criterion (plan.json, last FP-0021 acceptance line) now reads 'Keep the metadata language-neutral, with ownership, lifetime, thread, and error semantics expressed as data rather than C or Zig syntax.' FP-0029 adds 'Generate the selected language's raw declarations from the FP-0021 metadata, and extend that metadata through a reviewed schema change where it falls short.' FP-0021 no longer depends on a later selection.

docs/ABI_AND_WRAPPERS.md:79-81 defines the contract as 'the versioned C ABI and the process protocol'. Those lines also exclude the direct Zig API and bind a Zig first-party wrapper to the C ABI. ABI_AND_WRAPPERS.md:76, ARCHITECTURE.md:48, and the FP-0017 acceptance now say 'public embedding contract'. ARCHITECTURE.md:22 matches the definition. AGENTS.md:23 and ARCHITECTURE.md:93 remain consistent with it.
docs/QUALIFICATION.md:81 says such a shell 'fails both browser-product and embedding-wrappers qualification.'

FP-0023 adds 'Pin, build, and execute the first-party wrapper and the browser shell on actual Linux and macOS hosts through the public embedding contract.' Its allowed_paths now include 'bindings'. See R2 for a residual path gap.
FP-0018 adds 'Add each contract capability that the shell needs through a reviewed ABI schema change with C and first-party wrapper lifecycle tests, never through a shell-only entry point.'

FP-0029 allowed_paths now name 'toolchains/wrapper.lock.json' and 'engineering/dependencies.json' instead of the whole 'toolchains' directory, so zig.lock.json is no longer covered. A new criterion declares the toolchain and shipped runtime in a reviewed change to dependencies.json, separate from the wrapper implementation.

engineering/HANDOFF.md 'Owner decisions' records the first-embedder direction, the open language, and the FP-0029/FP-0017 wait. 'Environment facts' records 'Workers base on commit `1eae1f0` or later'. 'Actual state' points to ADR 0004 as proposed and awaiting the owner.
FP-0020 adds 'Expose broker decisions to the shell only through the public embedding contract, so every embedder receives the same containment.'
book/src/index.md:3 now reads 'a planned first-party Zig web engine with a minimal native browser.'
docs/TOOLCHAIN.md has a new 'First-party wrapper toolchain' section. The README.md:64 toolchains row mentions the future wrapper lock.

.omp/agents/fairpane-review.md:11 now rejects shell code outside the contract. .omp/agents/fairpane-platform.md:7 adds docs/ABI_AND_WRAPPERS.md to the platform agent's read list. AGENT_LAUNCH.md:39 now says 'before the first-party wrapper work starts'.
engineering/workstreams.json:85 and the FP-0017 gap criterion use the recommended wording.

evidence: This round changed no protected file. AGENTS.md, docs/CHARTER.md, and engineering/qualification.json still have the content I approved in review 1: 19 required capability ids, all with required:true.

Grepping for 'public C ABI', 'Zig API', and 'direct Zig' finds only uses that are consistent with the new definition. Those uses are AGENTS.md:23, ARCHITECTURE.md:22 and :93, ADOPTION_AND_GOVERNANCE.md:27 (an integration surface, not the contract), FP-0029's wrapper over the C ABI, and the protected embedding-wrappers description.

ADR 0004 (status: proposed, decision: pending) repeats the same contract definition and claims no language choice. The three evidence files it cites exist under engineering/evidence/wrapper-language/.
The dependency edges are unchanged. FP-0017 depends on FP-0006 and FP-0029, FP-0029 depends on FP-0021, and FP-0021 depends on FP-0006. There is no cycle.
state.json keeps FP-0029 'planned' with its owner-selection note.
No acceptance text claims the language is chosen.
The new sentences are complete and use American spelling.
The new FP-0018 and FP-0029 criteria are long but stay as single sentences.

findings.problem: engineering/policy.json lists 'toolchains' as a policy root. Writing toolchains/wrapper.lock.json therefore changes the policy digest. The dependencies.json criterion requires a separate reviewed change, but the pin criterion does not. AGENTS.md requires policy-affecting changes to stay separate from implementation.
findings.replacement: "Pin the selected language toolchain to exact versions and verified artifact digests in `toolchains/wrapper.lock.json`, through a reviewed change separate from the wrapper implementation."

findings.problem: FP-0023 now requires pinning the wrapper on Linux and macOS. Its allowed_paths do not include toolchains/wrapper.lock.json, and FP-0029 pins only for Windows execution.
findings.replacement: Add "toolchains/wrapper.lock.json" to FP-0023 allowed_paths. Alternatively, change the FP-0029 pin criterion to say "for every platform in `toolchains/zig.lock.json`".

findings.problem: FP-0029 may now 'extend that metadata through a reviewed schema change'. Its allowed_paths omit 'api' and 'include', the paths where FP-0021 is allowed to put the metadata and generated headers.

The definition leaves out the WebAssembly embedding. The protected embedding-wrappers capability (qualification.json:130) and the 'Process and WebAssembly boundaries' section treat that embedding as a public surface. I recommended this wording in review 1, so this nit corrects my own text.
findings.replacement: "The public embedding contract is the versioned C ABI, the process protocol, and the WebAssembly embedding for Wasm hosts."

findings.problem: Next action 1 freezes the FP-0029 contract while its prerequisite FP-0021 is still planned. AGENTS.md work procedure steps 2 and 3 select a task with accepted prerequisites before freezing it. Recording the owner's selection early is fine.
findings.replacement: "1. Record the owner's wrapper-language selection in ADR 0004. Freeze the `FP-0029` contract after `FP-0021` is accepted."

checks_main_agent_should_run: node tools/fairpane.mjs next (confirm that FP-0029 and FP-0017 are not listed as ready)
